under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed therewith, the High Court may be pleased to issue a writ or order, orders or directions more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus - i.declaring the action of the 12th respondent in compelling the petitioner to sit on the floor on 06-03-2025 despite her mothers explicit request to refrain the petitioner from such punishment due to the poor health condition and also the action of the 12th respondent in persisting to enforce the punishment despite hue and cry from the petitioner due to unbearable pain by giving deaf hearing to it and further, the action of the 12th respondent in continuously enforcing the punishment mercilessly despite receiving a specific request once again directly from the petitioners mother responding to the 12th respondents phone call upon informing that the petitioner is un-well and further the action of the respondents 1 to 7 in not acting upon petitioners representations/complaints dt.06-03-2025, 07-03-2025 and 09-03- 2025 as illegal, arbitrary, discriminative besides violative of Arts.14, 21 and 21-A, of the Constitution of India and ii.consequently, direct the respondents 1 to 7 to ensure that the 12th respondent does not interfere with petitioners education and examination process in any manner till completion of her final examinations in safe, peaceful and harassment-free environment Srk, J W.P.No.6143 of 2025 3 besides ensuring that the petitioner should not be subjected to any Mullu Mananya vs The State Of Ap texts.facts: (b) The petitioner was suffering from Typhoid, food poison etc., resulting in significant drop of platelets count, severe digestion issues and the petitioner was medically advised not to wear tight SRK, J clothing; that due to deteriorating health condition of petitioner and non-cooperation of 12th respondent, the petitioner was not sent to school for about one month; that though the petitioner was interested to attend school in spite of her poor health condition, 12th respondent did not allow her to attend classes in civil dress; that the petitioner and her parents were in fear of the attitude of 12th respondent in insisting the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class as punishment. (c) That upon the request made by the mother of petitioner, with great difficulty, 12th respondent gave permission to the petitioner, by allowing her to attend the school, in civil dress on health grounds for one day, and on the next day, 12th respondent refused to allow the petitioner and made her to sit separately on the floor as punishment; that on 05.03.2025, again the petitioner was forced to sit on the floor of the class, though the petitioner's mother requested not to do so and when the petitioner started crying, 12th respondent threatened her with dire consequences and caused humiliation to the petitioner. (d) That when the mother of petitioner along with her family friend viz. Nitta Swarna Latha, rushed to the school, 12th respondent remained adamant and refused to allow the petitioner SRK, J to sit on the bench, justifying it as disciplinary action; that 12th respondent placed her hand on the mother of petitioner and her family friend and dismissively told them to leave the school. Besides the above, it is the allegation of mother of petitioner that there is no Fitness Certificate and No Objection Certificate obtained from concerned departments. That the mother of petitioner gave complaint to the respondents and on 07.03.2025, both were called to the office of 5th respondent for Inquiry. Instead of cooperating with the process of Inquiry, 12th respondent deliberately escalated the situation by bringing around thirty (30) members to 5th respondent office and they shouted at the parents of petitioner, abused them and created an atmosphere of fear and intimidation. (e) That the respondent No.12, to divert the attention from her, instructed the staff members to spread a forwarded message and falsely portrayed 12th respondent as a victim in the hands of Mullu Mananya vs The State Of Ap on 11 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127175205/ 5 mother of petitioner, which act is a serious violation of ethical standards; that there is no spontaneous action either from the end of 5th respondent or from 3rd respondent, unless some preventive steps are taken by respondents, the unsafe environment would prevail and be continued against the petitioner. Hence, the Writ Petition. SRK, J 3. Respondent No.5 filed counter-affidavit, stating that on 06.03.2025, a complaint was received from the mother of petitioner, narrating the aforesaid issue and the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru was directed to conduct an Inquiry. In the Report submitted by the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru, it was stated that 12th respondent accepted that the petitioner was instructed to sit on the floor; that 12th respondent stated that only for discipline purpose, they instructed the students, who come late to school without uniform, to sit on the floor; that 12th respondent does not know about the severity of health condition of petitioner and that, she had no discrimination on any of the child; that 12th respondent tendered excuse for the mistake occurred, as she was unaware of illness of the petitioner at that time; that 12th respondent stated that the mother of petitioner and her family friend warned her over phone by some unknown persons and she would be imprisoned for two years. (b) A Show-Cause notice was issued vide Rc.No.1002/A1/ 2025, dated 07.03.2025 to the School Management regarding the issue; that 12th respondent in her reply stated that she was unaware of the health condition of the petitioner and the parents of the petitioner did not submit Medical Certificate to the school about SRK, J her illness; that 12th respondent was informed to allow the child to the school to attend examinations as per the direction of this Court and 12th respondent also gave assurance in that regard, but the petitioner and two other persons came to the District Educational Office and stated that they could not send the petitioner to school without any written statement from the school authority. Respondent No.6 conducted detailed Inquiry among 20 parents, who stated that it is not a big issue towards simple punishment. The parents of petitioners also accepted that there was no issue with the school for the past seven years. Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition. 4. Respondent No.12 filed counter-affidavit, denying the contents of the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petitioner, inter alia, contending that on 05.03.2025, the petitioner came to school late and as a disciplinary measure, she was instructed to sit on the floor for a limited period and later, she was allowed to sit on the bench along with other students, and this practice is being implemented in their school for several years and no parent raised objection or found fault with the Management therefor. That she noticed that the petitioner was feeling unwell and immediately, 12th respondent spoke to petitioner's mother and at that time, she did SRK, J not inform to 12th respondent that the petitioner was suffering from serious illness; that the mother of petitioner along with her friend Nitta Swarnalatha came to school, started shouting and started recording the entire incident through her mobile; that one of the Advocates called 12th respondent to her mobile and spoke to her in abusive language and insisted her to give unconditional apology and threatened her that she would be put in jail for two years if she did not do so. Mullu Mananya vs The State Of Ap on 11 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127175205/ 6 (b) That the parent of the petitioner and the persons who accompanied her on the date of the incident, were not in a position to listen to the words of 12th respondent and if really the petitioner is not well, she ought not to have been sent to school. If any student is found ill, the Management would inform the same to their parents and 12th respondent did the same. But the petitioner's mother in response to such intimation, approached the institution in a very high-handed manner. Respondent No.12 agreed before 10th respondent to tender apology stating that she was unaware about the health of the petitioner and to undertake that she would be more careful in future, but one Nitta Swarnalatha, who accompanied mother of petitioner, was not convinced with that, forced 12th respondent to sign on the apology letter drafted by her; SRK, J that 5th respondent called the parent and Management for Inquiry, on 07.03.2025 before the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru Division and even before the said authority, Nitta Swarnalatha, who accompanied petitioner's mother, shouted against 12th respondent using abusive language. The unwanted interference of persons, who accompanied petitioner's mother created the entire mess, which not only damaged the reputation of the institution but also spoiled the mind of the petitioner; that the action of petitioner's mother and her friend caused severe mental agony to 12th respondent. Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition with exemplary costs.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the entire incident occurred only due to the attitude of 12th respondent, as she insisted the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class towards punishment, though she is well aware of the fact that the petitioner was suffering from ill health. Learned counsel would further contend that during Inquiry before 5th respondent, the said authority witnessed the high-handed behaviour of 12th respondent with the parents of the petitioner and unless some preventive steps are taken by the respondents, the school environment, in which petitioner is studying, would continue against other pupils, who are SRK, J studying in the school; that the acts of 12th respondent caused humiliation to the petitioner and such adamant behaviour continued even after an Inquiry, being conducted by 5th respondent. 6. Learned Government Pleader for School Education representing respondent No.5 would contend that in the Inquiry conducted by 5th respondent, 12th respondent accepted that she instructed the petitioner to sit on the floor, as she came to school late and without proper uniform and such punishment is only for discipline purpose. Learned Government Pleader would further contend that 12th respondent tendered apology during Inquiry as she was unaware of illness of the petitioner, and stated she will be more careful in future. 7. Learned counsel for 12th respondent would contend that as the petitioner came late to the school and as a part of disciplinary measure, 12th respondent instructed the petitioner to sit on the floor for a limited period but the mother of petitioner along with her friend Nitta Swarnalatha raised objection and found fault with the said act and high-handedly rushed to the school premises and shouted over 12th respondent. Learned counsel would further contend that 12th respondent was threatened that she will be put in jail for two years if she did not tender apology. According to the SRK, J learned counsel, the entire incident occurred only due to high- handed approach of mother of petitioner and her family friend towards 12th respondent and their acts damaged the reputation of the school.
